zh.title: 達美航空48小時內發生兩起機艙煙霧緊急事件
zh.summary: 達美航空48小時內兩度遭遇機艙煙霧；乙架班機轉降，乙架優先降落，目前已展開調查。
body: 根據外媒 Simple Flying 報導，美國達美航空（Delta Air Lines）旗下航班於48小時內連續遭遇兩起機艙煙霧緊急事件。相關安全情況引發外界注意，該航空公司目前正針對兩起事件展開內部調查。
在發生的這兩起機艙煙霧事件中，受影響的航班分別採取了空中應變處置。其中乙架航班在出現機艙煙霧後執行了轉降程序，前往替代機場降落。
另一架遭遇機艙煙霧的達美航空航班則進行優先降落。航空公司目前正積極調查這兩起空中緊急事件的具體原因與詳細經過。

en.title: Delta Air Lines Investigates 2 Cabin Fume Emergencies In 48 Hours
en.summary: Delta Air Lines experienced two cabin fume emergencies in 48 hours, causing a diversion and priority landing.
body: Delta Air Lines has launched an investigation after two separate flights experienced cabin fume emergencies within a 48-hour period, according to a report by Simple Flying. The back-to-back inflight incidents required prompt operational emergency responses from the respective flight crews on board.

During the occurrences, one of the affected Delta flights was forced to execute an inflight diversion to another airport. Meanwhile, the second flight requested and completed a priority landing following the detection of cabin fumes.

Delta Air Lines is continuing to investigate both inflight incidents to determine what caused the cabin fume conditions. Further information regarding the root cause remains under technical assessment by the carrier.

zh.title: 泰國民航局率先採用波音CBTA訓練方案
zh.summary: 泰國民航局成為全球首個導入波音CBTA線上培訓的民航監理機關；波音於2026年9月1日公布
body: 泰國民航局（CAAT）成為全球首個將波音（Boeing）「能力本位訓練與評量」（CBTA）學習資料庫套用到整個國家飛行訓練體系的民航監理機關，並於2026年9月1日在亞太航空訓練高峰會期間發布。
這項合作將讓泰國各地的飛行學校能取得波音的CBTA學習內容，其設計目的是強化飛行員職能、提升訓練成效，並讓學員能更適應現代航空公司維運的需求。
波音表示，透過與國際公認的CBTA原則接軌，泰國飛行學校將能培育具備航空公司職涯所需的技術與行為技能的飛航人才。

en.title: Thailand's CAAT becomes first regulator to adopt Boeing's CBTA training solution
en.summary: Thailand's CAAT is first regulator to deploy Boeing's CBTA Learning Library; Boeing announced initiative on September 1, 2026
body: Thailand's Civil Aviation Authority of Thailand (CAAT) has become the first global aviation regulator to roll out Boeing's Competency-Based Training and Assessment (CBTA) Learning Library across an entire national flight training ecosystem, announced on September 1, 2026.

The initiative will give participating flight schools throughout the country access to Boeing's CBTA learning content, which is designed to strengthen pilot competencies, improve training effectiveness, and better prepare cadets for modern airline operations.

Boeing said that by aligning training with internationally recognized CBTA principles, Thai flight schools will be positioned to produce pilots with both the technical and behavioral skills required for airline careers.
